title: Ironhollow Rising Revisited
premise: Ines Iversen, the last apprentice of the Ledgerkeepers—a guild that trades in impossible things—has spent his life keeping accounts no one reads in a country that officially ceased to exist a decade ago. When a dying courier presses a map of the Doorway into his hands, Ines inherits both the guild's buried debt and the usurper's obsession, forcing him to flee with a disgraced knight and a smuggler who once loved him. As armies close on the free cities, Ines learns the Doorway is not an escape but a court: the old country's law still lives behind it, and it demands the usurper be judged. In the end, Ines chooses to stay outside the law he could have restored, sealing the Doorway with the guild's final entry so that justice must be built by living hands rather than inherited from dead ones.
about_author: Marguerite Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent seven years cataloguing the paperwork of dissolved governments before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about bureaucracy as magic and lives in a port city full of treaties nobody honors.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unread Pages
chapters.summary: Ines Iversen, POV. Ines balances the Ledgerkeepers' impossible accounts—bottled storms, borrowed years—while the free cities ignore their dying guild. A bleeding stranger collapses at the counting-house door and dies pressing a wax-sealed map into Ines's hands. Emotional beat: quiet dread; the safety of invisibility shatters in a single night.

chapters.title: What the Usurper Owes
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Deciphering the map, Ines finds entries in the guild's oldest ledger naming the usurper Aldric Vane as a debtor: he bought his crown on credit from the old country, and the Doorway is the collateral. Assassins arrive asking for the map by name. Emotional beat: fear curdling into resolve—he runs, but running is now a choice with a direction.

chapters.title: A Knight Without a Country
chapters.summary: Ser Brannoc Hale, POV. Brannoc, stripped of rank for refusing to burn a village, intercepts Ines on the salt road intending to rob him, then recognizes the guild seal and switches to protecting him—the old country once spared his family through its ledgers. Emotional beat: two people with nothing left but duty find an unexpected alignment.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Ines seeks passage from Wren Calloway, the smuggler he loved and betrayed years ago by choosing the guild over her. Wren agrees—for half the map's secret and his honesty about why he left. Emotional beat: love against duty made flesh; old wounds reopened under time pressure.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Sailing the drowned coast, Wren tests Ines's trust while hiding her own bargain: Vane's spymaster offered her amnesty for the map. She watches Ines quietly pay debts owed to strangers along the route and begins to doubt her deal. Emotional beat: guilt and tenderness entwined; corruption shown as small compromises.

chapters.title: The City That Signed Itself Away
chapters.summary: Brannoc, POV. The trio reaches Meridian Freeport, where the council debates surrendering to Vane. Ines publicly reads the ledger proving Vane's crown was purchased, not won—and the city's magistrates arrest him for sedition rather than face the truth. Emotional beat: fury and disillusionment; justice outside the law fails politely in public.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Broken out of jail by Wren and Brannoc, Ines realizes Vane's armies are days away and the Doorway lies across the Ashfen, where the guild's first founder sealed something worse than debt. Vane himself sends a letter offering Ines a place as his Royal Ledgerkeeper. Emotional beat: temptation; power offered as rescue, refused as rot.

chapters.title: Behind the Doorway
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Crossing the Ashfen, they open the Doorway and find the old country intact inside—its courts still sitting, its judges still waiting for the debtor king. But the court demands a price: whoever brings the case must remain as the country's final officer, forever. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by sacrifice; the map was never an exit, only a summons.

chapters.title: The Judgment of Aldric Vane
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Ines lures Vane to the Doorway with the one thing he cannot buy—forgiveness of his debt—and the old court convenes over the battlefield. Vane offers Ines co-rule of everything; Ines instead enters the evidence. The judges strip Vane's claim, and his army's loyalty dissolves with his legitimacy. Emotional beat: climax; love and duty reconciled as Wren and Brannoc hold the door while Ines speaks truth to power.

chapters.title: The Final Entry
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Refusing the judges' offer to become the old country's eternal keeper, Ines writes the guild's last ledger line and seals the Doorway, returning justice to the living world. He, Wren, and Brannoc walk back to free cities beginning to govern themselves without crowns or ledgers. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; Ines finally visible, ordinary, and free.
